summary: mymatasan now checks that it actually recorded. A new continuity monitor scores each closed hour of every recording-enabled camera against how much footage is really on disk, and raises a critical 'Recording gap' alert when a camera stops writing — then clears it when recording resumes. Until now nothing answered that question: the camera health monitor probes reachability, and a camera can be perfectly reachable while ffmpeg is wedged, the disk is full, the remux queue is quarantining every segment, or the stream URL silently changed. All of those recorded nothing and reported green, and an operator found out when somebody asked for footage of an incident. The Recordings page gains a coverage strip showing the last 7/30/90 days shaded by how complete each day is, backed by a new GET /api/recording/coverage endpoint — the same read model the monitor scores against, so the screen and the alert can never disagree. Care was taken to make it usable rather than noisy: only whole closed hours are scored, each hour is scored once regardless of sweep frequency, the default minimum is 95% (segment rollover and a recorder restart cost a few seconds an hour legitimately), the disk guard's recording pause suppresses per-camera alerts because it already raises its own, and a gap on a camera the health monitor knows is offline is attributed to that outage rather than reported as a second independent fault. Cameras with recording disabled — including detect-only AI frame sources — are never scored. Tunable from Settings > Camera health; new metrics mymatasan_recording_coverage_percent and mymatasan_recording_gap_cameras.
compatibility: Backward compatible, additive. New endpoints GET /api/recording/coverage and GET/PUT /api/settings/continuity; no schema changes and no migration (coverage is computed from existing recording_segment rows). The monitor defaults to ON, so existing installs begin checking after upgrade — expect alerts on cameras that genuinely have gaps. Thresholds are editable in Settings. Not yet live-benched: the acceptance test is to kill a camera's ffmpeg child and confirm the alert and the strip's hole appear.
